property_summary: After a Collect call, the caller's balance should not increase.
The total sum of all balances must not exceed total supply after any sequence of deposits and collects.
After a Collect call, the sum of the caller's balance and the withdrawn amount stays the same as before the call (i.e., balance decreases by exactly _am).
The balance of the caller never increases after Collect(msg.sender,...) is called
If a user deposits, the user's balance is at least the deposited amount.
After calling Collect, the total sum of balances plus the contract balance minus msg.value sent to user equals the sum of all deposits minus previous collects.

After any Collect call, the sum of all balances across all addresses (iterated over a fixed set of potential users) never exceeds the total ETH ever received by the contract (its initial balance plus all incoming transfers) minus the total ETH ever sent out via Collect.
After any Collect call, the balances of the caller are not increased compared to before the call.
After any sequence of calls ending with Collect, balances[msg.sender] decreases by the amount withdrawn (or stays the same if condition fails).
After Collect, the sum of all balances never decreases (i.e., totalSupply does not shrink) — the missing deduction causes it to stay the same or increase.
After Collect, the caller's balance decreases by the withdrawn amount when the condition holds.
After Collect, the balance of the sender is decreased by the withdrawn amount exactly when the withdrawal condition holds.
After Collect(uint256) returns without revert, the sum of all balances (via address(c).balance) remains unchanged from before the call.
After Collect succeeds, MinSum remains unchanged.
After any successful Collect call, MinSum equals its initial value set before initialization.
MinSum is never changed by a Collect call.
After a successful Collect call, MinSum equals the value set by SetMinSum before initialization.
After any call to Collect, MinSum equals the value that was set by SetMinSum before initialization.
After a call to Collect, the MinSum state variable remains unchanged (equal to its initial value).
After any call to Collect, the MinSum state variable never decreases.
After a successful call to Collect, the MinSum state variable is unchanged from its value before the call.
After any call to Collect, the value of MinSum is equal to its value before the call (i.e., Collect does not change MinSum).
After any call to Collect, the value of MinSum is equal to its value set during Initialized or SetMinSum, which is never modified by Collect.
After a Collect call, MinSum must remain unchanged because it is only set before initialization.
After Collect is called, MinSum must equal its initial value (0) because SetMinSum is the only way to change it and it is only callable before initialization.
After any call to Collect, MinSum is unchanged from its initial value (0) because SetMinSum can only be called before initialization.
After any call to Collect, MinSum must be less than or equal to the sum of all balances.
After a call to Collect, the MinSum value must be equal to its value before the call because no function called during Collect can change it.
After any Collect call, the MinSum value should have been set to its original value and not changed to 0 if initialization occurred.
After calling Collect, the MinSum state variable remains unchanged from its value before the call.
After any Collect call when the contract is initialized, MinSum remains equal to the value set during initialization, not zero.
After any Collect call, the MinSum value remains equal to the value set by SetMinSum before initialization.
After a Collect call, if the contract is initialized, MinSum retains its last set value (not zero).
After any Collect call, the MinSum state variable must remain unchanged.
After any sequence of calls ending in Collect, the value of MinSum remains equal to its initial value (0) because the reference contract does not modify MinSum.

After a Collect call that reverts due to insufficient balance, the MinSum state variable must remain at its most recently set value (which, in the reference, is always 0 because SetMinSum never changes it after initialization, and Collect never modifies MinSum). The buggy version unexpectedly changes MinSum inside SetMinSum when initialized, but since the reference never changes MinSum at all, any revert in Collect should leave MinSum unchanged.
After any call to Collect(uint256), the state variable MinSum must remain equal to its value before the call.
After any Collect call, the MinSum variable must be strictly less than its initial value plus the current block timestamp.
After setting the log file and calling Collect, the Log state variable in the contract is the address passed to SetLogFile, not a new instance.
The address stored in the Log state variable before and after a successful Collect call is the address that was set via SetLogFile.
After a call to Collect, the contract's balance of ether remains unchanged.
The Log address stored in the contract after a call to Collect(uint256) is the address passed to SetLogFile, provided that SetLogFile was called with a non-zero address.
After a call to Collect, the Log state variable's address equals the address passed to SetLogFile, not a newly created contract.
After a Collect call, the Log state variable (accessed via SetLogFile) must not be the zero address if Collect succeeded.
The Log state variable (accessed via SetLogFile) must remain unchanged after a Collect call, regardless of success or failure.
After a Collect call (success or revert), the stored Log address must be identical to the Log address before the call.
The address of the Log contract (returned by SetLogFile()) is never the zero address after a Collect call that doesn't revert.
After a Collect call, the SetLogFile() address must equal the LogFile address that was originally set.
After any call to Collect, the contract can always accept a deposit (Deposit does not revert) for the same caller.
After any Collect call, the caller's balance in the contract (balances[caller]) is exactly equal to the amount they previously deposited minus the amount they collected.
After a successful Collect call for a given address, the next Deposit call from that same address does not revert.
After any Collect call, calling Deposit with the same sender does not revert.
After a call to Collect that does not revert, the caller can always deposit at least the minimum sum (MinSum) without reverting.

After a call to Collect, the contract's balance is at least as much as the sum of all deposited amounts minus collected amounts, and the Deposits() function never reverts for any user with a positive balance.
After any Collect call, a user with positive balance can always call Deposit without reverting.
After any Collect call, the state variable MinSum remains unchanged.
After any Collect call, the sum of all recorded deposits in the Log contract (via History array lengths) should reflect the total value ever deposited through the Deposit function.
After any Collect call, for any user, calling Deposit with any positive amount does not revert.
After a Collect call by a user, the user's balance in the contract decreases by exactly the collected amount if the collection succeeds.
After a Collect call by a user, the user's balance in the contract is never less than the collected amount.
After a successful Collect call, the sum of all user balances in the mapping is never greater than the contract's ether balance minus the minimum sum threshold.

After a Collect call by any user, the total sum of all balances in the contract's balances mapping is less than or equal to the contract's ether balance plus the total ether ever deposited (via msg.value) during the test, minus the amount collected by that user if the collection succeeded.
After a Collect call, the contract's ether balance is never negative.
After a collect, the logged sender address in the last log entry equals the caller address.
After a Collect call, the stored sender address in the Log contract's last history entry equals the caller address.
After any Collect call, the Log contract's last History entry sender equals the caller address.
After a Collect call, the last log entry's sender is not address(0).
After a Collect call, the Log contract's history length remains unchanged (no new Log entry is added) if the call is made from an address other than msg.sender.
